Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the second chapter to unfold! The umpires have stepped onto the field and so are the players of Ireland. Jos Buttler and Phil Salt will be the opening pair for England. Ireland will start off with some spin as Matthew Humphreys will get the job to start with the new ball. Away we go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Update - 2.55 pm - The covers are off for the second time! The groundsmen have placed the stumps and the sun is glaring full-fledgedly. THE PLAY WILL RESUME AT 3.10 pm GMT with no over loss, and let's hope there are no more surprises from the rain gods!

Update - 2.43 pm GMT - Oh my word! Scratch the last update folks! It is pouring again and the covers sheets are placed once again on the pitch. A few moments ago, the sun was bright and glowy, but now it's all dark. The big sheets are coming on as well.

Update - 2.35 pm GMT - There's some chit chat going in the middle of the field between the match officials and the head groundsmen. Although the main cover is still firmly placed. The sun has started glazing on the field and the groundsmen are folding the main cover as well! The supper soppers are soaking the logged water around the outer field. We just got the confirmation, the PLAY WILL RESUME AT 2:50 pm GMT.
Update - 2.25 pm GMT - Positive news! The rain has finally relented, and the groundsmen are swiftly removing the sheets, one by one. Stay tuned for more updates.

Update - 2:19 pm GMT - Oh no... the weather isn't looking great folks! The groundsmen have done good job covering the track cause it's started drizzling in The Village, Malahide. Let's hope it's just a passing shower and the game resumes on time.

As The Three Lions prepare to embark on their run chase, the question lingers in the air - Can they successfully chase down the target, or will the Men in Greens' bowling unit rise to the challenge? The stage is set for a riveting second innings, where every run and wicket will shape the narrative of this encounter.

After losing four wickets in just nine overs for a mere 58 runs, Harry Tector and Benjamin Calitz stepped up to stabilize the innings. But it was Rashid who made the crucial impact once again, returning to the attack with the intent to dismantle the partnership. By the 15th over, Ireland found themselves struggling at 102 for 7. However, thanks to Gareth Delany's lightning-fast knock, they managed to post a competitive total on the scoreboard. In the wicket department, Adil Rashid led the charge with three wickets, while Jamie Overton and Liam Dawson each claimed two, and Rehan Ahmed contributed with one.

Ireland's openers got off to a solid start, expertly targeting debutant Sonny Baker from England and maximizing their scoring opportunities. However, their promising 30-run partnership was broken when the opposition skipper, Jacob Bethell, brought Liam Dawson into the attack. This pivotal moment allowed The Three Lions to ramp up the pressure. With @adil, the spin duo swiftly dismantled the top-order batters, which created a lot of pressure on the batting team.

What an exceptional inning it was from Gareth Delany! Ireland have put up a commendable score of 154 runs, but it was not looking possible if Delany hadn't stepped up. England were pretty well throughout the inning, but they leaked a lot of runs in the death over.

Commentary.Commentary: Back of a length, on middle and leg. Ross Adair flicks it toward deep mid-wicket and gets a couple of runs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.3: Sonny Baker to Ross Adair, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Excellent comeback from the youngstar! Full-length delivery, on middle, angling it in sharply. Ross Adair, with no footwork, tries to flick it away but gets beaten on the inner edge and thumps on the pad.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.2: Sonny Baker to Ross Adair, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! BOOMBASTIC! The first biggie of the inning! Sonny Baker pitches it up, on off, shaping it in. Ross Adair golfs it over long off fence for half a dozen.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.1: Sonny Baker to Ross Adair, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: Short of a length, on middle. Ross Adair hangs back and tucks it toward sqaure leg for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.6: Luke Wood to Ross Adair, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Hard-length delivery, on middle. Ross Adair attempts to swat it over mid-wicket but gets beaten on the inner edge.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.5: Luke Wood to Ross Adair, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Back of a length, around middle. Ross Adair clips it toward the leg side.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.4: Luke Wood to Ross Adair, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Leg bye! Back of a length, on middle and leg, swings in a bit. Paul Stirling misses his nudge and thumps his thigh pad. The ball rolls away toward the leg side and the batter takes the single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.3: Luke Wood to Paul Stirling, Leg bye.

Commentary.Commentary: On a length, on middle. Paul Stirling nudges it toward mid-wicket for no run.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.2: Luke Wood to Paul Stirling, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! SHOT! Exceptional from Paul Stirling! Much fuller, angling it wide across the line. Paul Stirling's eyes light up watching the width of the ball. He extends his arms and launches it over the cover region for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.1: Luke Wood to Paul Stirling, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Who will operate from the other end? Luke Wood it is!
FOUR! CLASS! Ross Adair is off the mark in style! Full-length delivery, outside off. Ross Adair uses his bottom hand and lashes it over the extra cover fielder for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.6: Sonny Baker to Ross Adair, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Swing and a miss! Fuller, pitching it outside off and swings it in. Ross Adair looks to punch it away but gets beaten on the inner edge.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.5: Sonny Baker to Ross Adair, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: A width to offer, on a good length, outside the seventh stump. Paul Stirling frees his arms and punches it uppishly, over the cover region. But the ball slows down around the deep cover fence due to the slow outfield. The deep backward point fielder does well to sprint to his right and dives to save the boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.4: Sonny Baker to Paul Stirling, 3 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Good-length delivery, around off. Paul Stirling drives it toward the fielder in the cover region.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.3: Sonny Baker to Paul Stirling, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: WIDE! Ireland are underway with that bonus run. On a length, pitching it on middle, but swaying it down the leg. Paul Stirling tries to flick but misses.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.3: Sonny Baker to Paul Stirling, Wide!

Commentary.Commentary: Pitches it up this time, outisde off, shaping it in. Paul Stirling shuffles and attempts to flick it uppishly, but misses the connection and thumps his pad.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.2: Sonny Baker to Paul Stirling, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Excellent start of the spell! Bowls it back of a length, pitching it outside off, around seventh stump and nips it a shy bit away from the batter. Paul Stirling lunges and goes for a drive but gets beaten on the swing.

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set for the action to begin! The umpires have taken their position and the players of Ireland have scattered to their respective fielding positions. The skipper, Paul Stirling, will be opening with Ross Adair for Ireland. Sonny Baker gets the job to start with the new ball. A big day for the debutant. Time to play...

We are moments away from the first ball of this contest, but before that, Jacob Bethell and Paul Stirling lead their respective sides out for the national anthems. It will be England's national anthem first, followed by that of Ireland.

PITCH REPORT - Isabella Joyce is pitchside with the insights. Starts off saying there is a bit of grass covered on the pitch so the seamers will get some bounce. Also, say that it seems like it's a batting pitch.

The skipper of Ireland, Paul Stirling, says that there's a bit grass on the track, therefore they are ready to face the bouncers from the pacers. Continues that they weren't far away from winning the match, but they need to stop losing wickets. Ends up saying that Benjamin Calitz is all set to make his debut and Ben White joins the line up as well.

Jacob Bethell, skipper of England, says that bowling first is the best way to win cricket in this venue. Continues that he enjoyed playing the first match and they would try to replicate the same in this match as well. It ends up saying that they have two changes in the lineup, with Jordan Cox coming in and Sonny Baker ready to make his debut.

England (Playing XI) - Phil Salt, Jos Buttler (WK), Jacob Bethell (C), Jordan Cox (In place of Sam Curran), Rehan Ahmed, Tom Banton, Jamie Overton, Liam Dawson, Adil Rashid, Luke Wood, Sonny Baker (In place of Will Jacks).

Ireland (Playing XI) - Paul Stirling (C), Ross Adair, Harry Tector, Lorcan Tucker (WK), Curtis Campher, Benjamin Calitz (In place of George Dockrell), Gareth Delany, Barry McCarthy, Matthew Humphreys, Craig Young, Ben White (In place of Graham Hume).
TOSS - England have won the toss and elected to BOWL first.

The weather forecast is a bit uncertain, so let's hope the rain stays away and we get a full game in. So grab your snacks, get comfortable, and get ready for what promises to be an epic final showdown. Toss and team news in a bit...

Both teams showed some serious firepower with the bat in the opening game. Ireland posted a formidable total of 196, thanks to impressive half-centuries from Lorcan Tucker and Harry Tector. England, however, chased it down with ease, led by a blistering 89 from Phil Salt. We're expecting another high-scoring encounter with plenty of big hits and exciting plays.

Welcome to The Village in Dublin for the third and final T20I between England and Ireland! The series is on the line today after a thrilling first match and a rain-abandoned second. England currently leads 1-0, but the Irish side will be looking to bounce back and level the series in front of their home crowd.
... MATCHDAY ...

All roads lead to Malahide for the decider as Ireland and England gear up for the 3rd T20I after the second game was washed out, leaving the series delicately poised. England looked ruthless in the opener with Phil Salt’s explosive 89 leading a dominant chase, while Jos Buttler and their deep batting order remain a constant threat, along with the all-round skills of Sam Curran, who is enjoying his return to the national side. Their bowling attack, combining Adil Rashid’s guile with the pace of Jamie Overton and Luke Wood, gives them balance across conditions. Ireland, though, will take heart from their batting efforts in the first match, where Harry Tector and Lorcan Tucker shone, and captain Paul Stirling remains the key to setting the tone at the top. The big question for them will be if their bowlers can hold their nerve against England’s power-hitters, especially at the death, where they leaked plenty. With Ireland aiming to level the series and England pushing for another statement win ahead of bigger challenges, fans can expect a gripping contest to close out the series.
